col.method: Internal, not an operator comparison. Available vehicles (not disabled, not reserved) of the selected fleet are checked against the operator's own GBFS geofencing zones, in two kinds. No-parking zone: ride end, riding or riding through prohibited; excluded are mandatory parking zones, permitted areas inside the no-parking zone that are smaller than it (e.g. a mobility hub; an operating zone lifts nothing) and vehicles ≤ {stationM} m from one of the operator's stations. Mandatory parking zone without station: zone with station_parking (parking only at stations) and no own station ≤ {mpzStationM} m ({stationM} m station distance + GPS surroundings); {stationM}–{mpzStationM} m counts as just next to the station and is only counted. A vehicle is listed only if the 4 points at {buffers} m (north, east, south, west) also lie in a prohibited area or a mandatory parking zone: this filters out GPS inaccuracy and vehicles at the zone edge. Limits: the data has no rules per vehicle type; a zone may be newer than the parking; idle times since the start of measurement are lower bounds (≥).

ops.seqTitle: Same stops, different order: pure priority order = most urgent stop first regardless of the way; nearest neighbour = always to the closest stop. “Priority” = extra km compared with the shortest run and the priority-weighted mean distance to the stops (this run instead of the shortest run).
ops.osrmUnreachable: OSRM not reachable: km by straight line × 1.35, next attempt in 2 min at the earliest
ops.orderPerRunPrio: Order per run: objective = distance + λ × priority-weighted mean distance to the stops (Σ wᵢ·dᵢ ÷ Σ wᵢ; dᵢ = km from the depot to stop i, wᵢ = priority − lowest priority of the run). λ comes from the “priority ↔ distance” slider ({levels}): λ = 1 means reaching the urgent stops 1 km earlier is worth a 1 km detour; λ = 0 is pure kilometre optimisation, as are equal priorities. Up to {exactMax} stops per group exact (Held-Karp), above that nearest neighbour (plain and with priority), pure priority order and further start points, each improved with 2-opt and Or-opt on the full objective. Rebalancing and station balancing: first all pickups, then all drop-offs, both optimised together. Kilometres with “road routing” (default): road matrix of the OSRM demo server (without traffic; up to {osrmMax} points per request, cached, at most one request per second), driving time from the driven route; without road routing or on failure straight line × {detour} at {speedKmh} km/h. The time limit applies to planning, by road a run may exceed it slightly (marked). On-site times: 1.5 min pick up, 1 min drop off, 2.5 min battery, 3 min workshop.
ops.prioValues: Priority per stop (0 = not urgent, 1 = urgent, up to 1.5 with surcharge): battery swap {energyW} × energy gap (1 − charge ÷ threshold or 1 − range ÷ threshold, the larger) + {idleW} × idle time (full from {idleRefH} h); pickup and workshop: idle time or time disabled (full from {idleRefH} h); from {longIdleH} h +{longIdleBonus} each. Drop-off: shortfall ÷ {needRef} (at most 1), spot without an available vehicle nearby or empty station +{emptyBonus}; pickup at a full station {fullStation}, otherwise 0. A stop with several vehicles counts with the most urgent one. The run card shows priority, rank and reason per stop, plus the km compared with pure priority order and nearest neighbour.

ops.uncertaintyText: Starts and ends are counts (Poisson). Balancing: Σ starts and Σ ends of a municipality should be equal but are not: deployments and returns from the warehouse count as ends, trips across the municipal boundary and at the edge of the measurement window only on one side (31/10–01/11/2026 without gap bands: Stuttgart 11 %, Frankfurt 10 % more ends than starts). The ends of each municipality are therefore multiplied by k = Σ starts ÷ Σ ends. The sums include the suppressed events (cell × band below 3, per municipality only as a sum), which are not assigned to any cell. Afterwards net outflow across the whole municipality is 0 and shows where vehicles leave faster than on average. Starts stay unchanged; the surplus ends are assumed to be distributed like the other ends. Standard error = √(starts + k² × ends) ÷ measured hours, range = net ± {z} × standard error. The MCDA uses the cautious lower bound max(0, net − {z} × standard error); the need uses the estimate. Stability: in addition to the ±20 % weight sensitivity, the starts and ends of every cell are redrawn {draws} times (Poisson bootstrap with a fixed seed: same input, same result); each draw recomputes balancing, standardisation and ranking. “Stable” means: the spot stays among the top spots in all weight variants and in at least {minShare} % of the draws; below that it is “uncertain” with the share.
ops.swapRangeRule: Range relative to the source: some feeds report only small ranges (Lime via MobiData BW: at most ≈ 14 km); with “below {std} km” a third of their scale would count as empty. Per source with at least {minN} ranges the threshold is therefore min(form value, {share} % of the 95th percentile of the range) if the 95th percentile is below {maxP95} km; otherwise the form value. {share} % matches the charge-level threshold, {maxP95} km × {share} % = {std} km (continuous transition). The threshold is shown in the feed check and per vehicle in ops/<state>.json (reichweiteSchwelleKm). If the range is calculated from the battery level, only the battery level counts as before. If a source reports the same range for almost all vehicles (placeholders such as Donkey Bavaria 1 km or nextbike 0 km: over 95 % identical values or a p5–p95 spread below 0.1 km), its range does not count; without a usable battery level the energy is then unknown, not low.

ops.perCell250MAndTimeOfDayBand: Per cell ({CELL}) and time-of-day band the collector counts trip starts (available vehicle disappears or stable ID departs) and trip ends (vehicle appears or arrives) every 20 minutes across all operators (market); runs after a gap of more than 45 minutes do not count. Net outflow = (starts − k × ends) ÷ measured hours, k balances Σ starts and Σ ends of the municipality (see uncertainty and stability): positive means more vehicles leave the cell than arrive, it needs supply; negative means vehicles accumulate (a source for rebalancing). Standard error, range and lower bound are shown below each value. The operator gets its current share of the available fleet in the municipality. From 02/11/2026, origin–destination flows (flows/<day>.json, only operators with stable IDs, rows from 2 trips) additionally confirm outflow and inflow per cell: shown is for how many spots with net outflow the flows also show more departures than arrivals. Below {prelimH} measured hours, net outflow and stability are preliminary.
ops.needMax0NetOutflowHHorizon: Need = max(0, net outflow/h) × horizon (default {horizonH} h) + base stock; base stock = trip starts/h × {baseH} h, because starts and ends do not arrive at the same time. Rounded up, at least {minPerSpot}, at most {maxPerSpot} vehicles per spot. Fleet = the operator's available vehicles now within {spotRadiusM} m (the surroundings count, not just the coordinate). Shortfall = need − fleet. Example: 2.0 starts/h and 1.2 ends/h → net 0.8/h × 3 h + 2.0 = 4.4 → need 5; 2 vehicles nearby → shortfall 3.
ops.factorsStandardisedTo0195th: Factors standardised to 0–1 (95th percentile as upper bound, direction: more = better): net outflow as the cautious lower bound max(0, net − 2 × standard error) (inflow and uncertain outflow = 0), demand (starts/h), public transport proximity (stop points ≤ 200 m, 3 = full), parking area (e-scooter parking bay, official area or sharing hub ≤ 160 m = 1, bike rack ≤ 80 m = 0.5). Net outflow replaces the former “undersupply” (starts ÷ fleet), which was only derived. Whether demand and net outflow measure the same thing is shown by the rank correlation ρ across the candidate cells above the spot table (whole day, as of 01/11/2026: Stuttgart 0.13, Berlin 0.24, Duisburg 0.21 – the two factors measure different things, no double counting). The spot snaps to the area. No-parking zones from the operator's GBFS zones are an exclusion, not a weight; so are the city's official no-parking zones (Berlin: micromobility no-parking zones, Munich: geofences within 100 m of the parking areas), unless the spot lies on a designated parking area. Official parking areas (Berlin, Munich) count like e-scooter parking bays; source and licence are shown above the spot table and in the legend. In mandatory parking zones (GBFS station_parking, e.g. Dott Leipzig) the spot snaps to the operator's nearest station (≤ 150 m); without a station the cell drops out. Minimum distance between spots.
ops.saatyScale1EquallyImportant3: Saaty scale (1 = equally important, 3 = somewhat more important, 5 = clearly more important; row against column). Net outflow 2× demand: outflow is the direct reason to refill, demand ensures the spot is used. Weights = principal eigenvector, λmax = {lambdaMax}, consistency ratio CR = {cr} (< 0.10; verified with numpy). If a factor is missing (e.g. OSM unreachable), it is left out and the remaining weights are renormalised. Sensitivity: each weight ±20 %, renormalised; “stable” = spot stays in the selection in all variants, “medium” ≥ 75 %, otherwise “uncertain”.
ops.rebalanceSurplusMeans: Rebalance: surplus means vehicles above the need of their cell, vehicles not moved for over 24 h and extra vehicles at spots; batteries below {minBatteryForMove} % are not moved but swapped. Surplus per cell follows the same need formula. Priority by shortfall: the spot with the largest shortfall gets the nearest surplus vehicles first (≤ {v1} km) and opens a run first; R1 covers the largest shortfall. Collect first, then drop off. Battery swap: only if charge is below {swapThreshold} % and range below {swapRangeKm} km (values in the form; if a feed reports only one of them, that one decides). Priority = 0.6 × energy gap + 0.4 × demand at the location, at most 50 batteries per run. Workshop: disabled vehicles, longest disabled first. Stations: refill stations at ≤ 20 % fill from stations at ≥ 80 % to 50 %.
ops.bundlingByAreaOpenJob: Bundling by area: the open job farthest from the depot opens a run (rebalancing: the job for the spot with the largest shortfall, on a tie the farthest), then the jobs nearest to the run's centre are added until capacity is reached (rebalancing: centre of pickup and destination). If the run takes longer than the set time (default {v0} h, driving + on site), it keeps the most nearby jobs that still fit; the distant ones go back and form their own runs. Anything beyond the number of runs per type is listed as “not scheduled” at the run list.
ops.orderPerRunNearestNeighbour: Order per run: nearest neighbour from six start points, then 2-opt and Or-opt on a distance matrix of the run; each move is evaluated over the changed edges (with asymmetric road costs using forward and backward sums), the result is the same as with the full run calculation. With “road routing” (default) the order is optimised by vehicle kilometres on the road (OSRM distance matrix), km and driving time come from the driven route (OSRM demo server, without traffic); the time limit applies to planning, by road a run may exceed it slightly (marked). Without road routing or on failure: straight line × 1.35 at {speedKmh} km/h. On-site times: 1.5 min pick up, 1 min drop off, 2.5 min battery, 3 min workshop.
ops.idleTimeCountsFromFirst: Idle time counts from the first sighting by the collector. Operators with rotating IDs produce more starts and destinations than real trips; for them, demand should be read relatively. Suppressed demand (nobody finds a vehicle) is not measured. The operator's deployments with new IDs count as trip ends: at its own deploy places, net outflow is therefore a lower bound. Parking areas and stop points from OpenStreetMap are as complete as the map. With a new collector snapshot, Operations recalculates with the new fleet as soon as it is shown.
